summary.en: Delta Air Lines' automated weight-and-balance system failed on Sunday morning, prompting the Federal Aviation Administration to impose a ground stop on Delta flights bound for Atlanta at the airline's request, later downgraded to a ground delay programme averaging about 57 minutes. More than 360 flights were delayed at Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport, and by 11 am ET, 591 Delta flights nationwide were delayed. Delta said its teams were using manual workarounds to get flights departed while the automated system is restored. The disruption comes days before Thanksgiving, one of the busiest travel periods of the year at the world's busiest airport.

summary.en: Chief Executive John Lee said the Election Committee subsector ordinary elections were successfully held and congratulated all elected members on behalf of the SAR Government. The Election Committee comprises 1,500 members from 40 subsectors; in this election, 31 of 36 subsectors were contested, with 856 candidates vying for 723 seats, in what Lee described as healthy competition among patriots who are committed, capable and effective. The new Election Committee takes office on February 1 next year for a five-year term. Lee urged all members to fulfil their duties under the principle of patriots administering Hong Kong and help implement Hong Kong's first five-year plan, and thanked voters, the Electoral Affairs Commission and all staff involved.

summary.en: Law Society president Roden Tong was the only candidate to lose in the legal sector, as 16 candidates contested 15 seats; he received 19 votes, while the Law Society's three council members were all elected with high votes. Tong said winning and losing are normal and there is nothing to make a fuss about, and suggested his defeat may be linked to pushing various reforms and possibly to the Law Society's earlier proposal that solicitor advocates be eligible to become Senior Counsel, saying many people think that is the reason. Newly elected Senior Counsel Ronny Tong said he was surprised by the result, describing the defeat as more political than a question of legal standing; LegCo member Priscilla Leung praised Roden Tong's work and his contributions to the legal profession.

summary.en: Vote counting for the Election Committee subsector ordinary elections finished at 10:15 pm, with Electoral Affairs Commission chairman Justice Lok Kai-hong saying the voting and counting went very smoothly and the arrangements embodied the principles of openness, honesty and fairness. Of the 31 contested subsectors, 723 candidates were elected; 259 candidates in the five uncontested subsectors were returned unopposed, and 156 members were nominated by 40 designated bodies. A total of 5,640 voters cast ballots, a cumulative turnout of 98.79%, and counting took about three hours and 45 minutes. The commission is satisfied with the overall arrangements and will review them as required by law and report to the Chief Executive; the official register of Election Committee members will be published on February 1 next year.

summary.en: The developer of the luxury One Stanley housing estate in Stanley says it has reported an alleged extortion attempt to police. K&K Property said it reported the matter on November 4; the firm was reportedly asked to pay tens of millions of Hong Kong dollars, with the alleged extorter threatening to disclose information believed to be damaging to the company. A company spokesman said the case had been handed to police and declined further comment. One Stanley came under scrutiny last month after allegations of substandard steel reinforcement work, and the developer's subsidiary K Wise has offered homeowners a six-year structural warranty and free independent property inspections.

summary.en: ICAC Commissioner Woo Ying-ming departed for Marrakech, Morocco today to chair the International Association of Anti-Corruption Authorities' annual conference and general assembly as its president, and to stand for the association's next presidency on behalf of the ICAC. The conference marks the IAACA's 20th anniversary and brings together anti-corruption experts, government officials, international organisation representatives and academics from around the world to share the latest anti-corruption strategies. ICAC officers will also host a seminar on using artificial intelligence to fight corruption. Woo returns to Hong Kong on November 26.

summary.en: The Centre for Health Protection is investigating a case of invasive meningococcal infection involving a 74-year-old man with underlying illness. He developed a fever and malaise on November 19, saw a private doctor the next day and was admitted to Kwong Wah Hospital the same day as his condition worsened; he is now stable and his cerebrospinal fluid tested positive for meningococcus, with a clinical diagnosis of meningitis. He had no travel history during the incubation period, his family members are asymptomatic and have been given preventive drugs, and the case is believed to be sporadic. Six cases have been recorded so far this year, against 11 last year.

summary.en: The grand finale outdoor carnival of the Asia+ Festival 2026, "Asian Ethnic Cultural Performances+", was held this afternoon at the Hong Kong Cultural Centre Piazza and Foyer, with around 30 Belt and Road countries and regions presenting their diverse cultures through ethnic music, dance, handicrafts and signature snacks, attracting over 33,000 members of the public and tourists. Secretary for Culture, Sports and Tourism Rosanna Law said the festival provides a platform for artistic exchanges and reaffirms Hong Kong's role as an East-meets-West centre for international cultural exchanges. The "Convergence of Cross-Cultural Gifting - Ethnic Cultural Exhibition" runs at the Cultural Centre Foyer until November 29.

summary.en: Voting in the Election Committee Subsector Elections has closed, and Electoral Affairs Commission chairman Lok Kai-hong said more than 5,600 voters cast ballots for a turnout above 98%, with all ballot boxes delivered to the central counting station at the Convention and Exhibition Centre and results expected to be announced progressively soon. Lok said he would not comment on the turnout figure, but was encouraged by it and believed it showed Hong Kong's electoral system operating with growing maturity. The commission had received one complaint about election advertising as of 6pm and was handling it.

summary.en: Voting in the 2026 Election Committee Subsector Ordinary Elections closed at 6pm today, with 5,640 registered voters casting ballots for a provisional cumulative turnout of about 98.79%, well above the 89.77% recorded in 2021. summary.en: Gulf stock markets fell in early trading on Sunday as Middle East tensions continued to weigh on sentiment. Saudi Arabia's benchmark index slipped 1.7%, with Al Rajhi Bank down 2% and Saudi National Bank, the country's largest lender, down 1.8%; Qatar's market fell 1.5% with nearly all shares in the red, including Qatar Islamic Bank down 1.3%; Bahrain dropped 0.4%. The declines followed Iran's claim that its air defences hit a US F-16 fighter jet over the Gulf, which Washington denied, saying all American warplanes in the Middle East are safe. A Qatari delegation visited Tehran on Friday to mediate, and Iran's foreign minister said Tehran still hopes to end the war through diplomacy.

summary.en: Hong Kong Customs detected two drug trafficking cases involving baggage concealment at Hong Kong International Airport on November 20 and 21, seizing about 37.3kg of suspected cannabis buds with an estimated market value of about $8 million. In the first case, a 46-year-old British transit passenger arriving from Bangkok and bound for London was found with about 35kg in two check-in suitcases. In the second, about 2.3kg was found in unclaimed baggage from Bangkok on August 10; a 39-year-old Mainland man was arrested yesterday on arrival via Taipei. Both men have each been charged with trafficking in a dangerous drug and will appear at West Kowloon Magistrates' Courts tomorrow (November 23).

summary.en: South Korean Education Minister Choi Kyo-jin said he is resigning after the government's handling of cheating prevention for the national college entrance exam caused chaos and inconvenience for candidates and the public, and President Lee Jae-myung has accepted his resignation. summary.en: Secretary for Labour and Welfare Chris Sun Yuk-han has pledged that support for victims of the Wang Fuk Court fire will continue for the long term, with trauma and mental health care for the bereaved and seriously injured potentially lasting "years, even decades". summary.en: The Election Committee subsector ordinary election is held today, with 31 subsectors contested and 856 candidates vying for 723 seats among about 5,700 eligible voters. The social welfare subsector is the most competitive, with 25 candidates chasing 15 seats, or 1.66 candidates per seat.
